chunks: You know that what we did was not a competition for power, nor seeking anything from the vanities of the world, but rather to restore the signs of Your religion and to manifest reform in Your lands, so that the oppressed among Your servants may be safe and the suspended commands of Yours may be established.
ai.seo_question: What was the true motivation for accepting political authority in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this foundational text from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali articulates the theological justification for his caliphate, distinguishing it from the worldly ambitions of his predecessors. He emphasizes that his primary objective was to revive the dormant symbols of Islam (Ma'alim al-Din) and establish justice (Adl) for the oppressed, thereby fulfilling the divine mandate to implement Sharia. This statement serves as a key Shia argument for the legitimacy of the Ahl al-Bayt's rule based on religious revival rather than political conquest.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Thou knowest that what we did was not to seek power nor to acquire anything from the vanities of the world, We rather wanted to restore the signs of Thy religion and to usher prosperity into Thy cities so that the oppressed among Thy creatures might be safe and Thy forsaken commands might be established.
